brief:
A religious authority's statement against Palestinian participation in Israel's government has reignited concerns about political extremism in the country, drawing comparisons to the 1995 assassination of Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin. The ruling has intensified hostility toward Palestinians holding government positions, according to Al Jazeera English.

The comparison reflects deeper anxieties about far-right political violence in Israel. Rabin was killed by a right-wing extremist opposed to his peace negotiations with Palestinians, an event that marked a turning point in Israeli politics and remains a potent symbol of the dangers posed by incitement against political opponents.
dek: Hostility towards Palestinian participation in Israel's government fuels fears of far-right political violence.
title: Religious ruling stokes Israeli fears of far-right violence
